literal: what is fitting; the true course

definitions.definition: The true order that holds together the cosmos (the courses of sun, dawn, seasons and waters), the sacrifice and right conduct; guarded by Varuṇa and Mitra; born with satya from kindled tapas (RV 10.190.1); the twelve-spoked wheel of the year is 'the wheel of ṛta' (1.164.11).

equivalents.note: The later tradition speaks of dharma where the Saṃhitās speak of ṛta and dharman (RV 1.164.50 calls the first sacrifices 'the first dharmas'); the scope differs (ṛta is also cosmic order).

notes: Scholarly metadata only (not used in interpretation): cognate of Avestan aṣ̌a/arta.

definitions.definition: Truth, the real and the truthful word; upholds the earth (RV 10.85.1; AVŚ 12.1.1); the vow-taker passes 'from untruth to truth' (VS 1.5); Varuṇa's fetters bind the untruthful and release the truth-speaker (AVŚ 4.16.6).

equivalents.note: Paired in RV 10.190.1 and AVŚ 12.1.1; satya stresses the real and the spoken truth, ṛta the order.

definitions.definition: Untruth and violation of ṛta; what Varuṇa's fetters punish (AVŚ 4.16.6); even sleep does not keep it away (RV 7.86.6).

Generative heat and ascetic effort: That One was born by the power of tapas (RV 10.129.3); ṛta and satya were born from kindled tapas (10.190.1); the ancients reached heaven by tapas (10.154.2); the seers first undertook tapas and dīkṣā (AVŚ 19.41.1); the one whose body is unheated does not attain soma (RV 9.83.1).

The sacrifice: offering into fire to the gods with mantra, the rite that sustains gods and world; the gods first sacrificed the Puruṣa, 'sacrificing to the sacrifice with the sacrifice' (RV 10.90.16).

cross_language.note: reinterpreted as giving and virtue in the Pali texts

notes: Scholarly metadata only (not used in interpretation): cognate of Avestan yasna.

definitions.definition: What upholds; an ordinance or foundation; the first sacrifices were 'the first dharmas' (RV 10.90.16 = 1.164.50); the dead go to heaven and earth 'according to dharman' (10.16.3).
The binding ordinance of a god (Varuṇa 'of firm vratas'), and a vow undertaken by a person ('Agni, lord of vows, I shall undertake the vow', VS 1.5).

The consecration that makes the sacrificer fit for the soma rite, with restraint, vigil and tapas; with tapas it is among the powers that uphold the earth (AVŚ 12.1.1) and was first undertaken by the seers (AVŚ 19.41.1).
Faith and trust that the offering reaches its end: by faith the fire is kindled and the oblation offered (RV 10.151); 'have faith in him — he is Indra' (2.12.5).
The sacrificial fee and gift to the priests; the givers of gifts stand high in heaven and partake of immortality (RV 10.107.2).
Giving of wealth and food; the giver's wealth does not waste away, and 'who eats alone has only sin' (RV 10.117).

literal: what is sacrificed and what is given

definitions.definition: The accumulated merit of sacrifices and gifts, with which the dead are reunited in the highest heaven (RV 10.14.8).

literal: the world of those who have done well

definitions.definition: The heavenly world to which Agni carries the dead man's unborn part (RV 10.16.4).
An offence, especially against the gods' ordinances, which the worshipper asks Varuṇa to loosen like a rope (RV 2.28.5).
Sin as a burden or stain, one's own or inherited from the fathers, from which Varuṇa is asked to release (RV 7.86.5, 7.89.5).
Freed from offence 'before Aditi', the state asked of Varuṇa when his fetters are loosened (RV 1.24.15).
Distress or anxiety, from which Rudra and the gods are asked to set one free (RV 2.33.2).
The fetter of Varuṇa (or of death, Nirṛti) that binds the offender (RV 1.24.15, 7.88.7; AVŚ 4.16.6).
Skill and effective will; Vasiṣṭha pleads that his fault was 'not my own will (dakṣa)' (RV 7.86.6); Dakṣa is also the god born of Aditi (10.72.4).
The auspicious, prayed for in intention, hearing and seeing (RV 1.89.1, 1.89.8).
Concord of mind among people, the subject of RV 10.191.
Harmony in family and community, produced by the Atharvavedic concord hymns (AVŚ 3.30).
A good deed; the dead go to the world of those who have done well (RV 10.16.4).
'The One Being the inspired call by many names' (RV 1.164.46).

equivalents.note: Both name the One of the speculative hymns; 1.164.46 speaks of the One named by the gods' names, 10.129 of That One before creation.

definitions.definition: That One which breathed windless by its own power before creation (RV 10.129.2), was born by tapas (10.129.3), and 'has become all this' (8.58.2).

equivalents.note: Vedānta reads That One as Brahman; the hymn itself does not name it, and the ritual (Mīmāṃsā) reading posits no such single referent.

definitions.definition: Being; in RV 10.72 'being was born from non-being'; in 10.129 before creation 'there was neither non-being nor being'.
Non-being or the non-existent, in which the seers found the bond of being (RV 10.129.4); from it being was born (10.72.2–3).

equivalents.note: Śaṅkara reads the asat of creation texts as the unmanifest (unmanifested name and form), not absolute nothing; the Saṃhitā does not say so.

definitions.definition: Inherent power by which That One breathed (RV 10.129.2) and the immortal moves (1.164.38); also the call and food offered to the fathers, who rejoice in svadhā (10.14.7).
That which was covered by the void before That One was born by tapas (RV 10.129.3); its sense (life-force, emptiness, the germ) is debated by commentators.
The undistinguished water that 'all this' was in the beginning (RV 10.129.3); the great waters that bore the germ (10.121.7).
Seed; desire was 'the first seed of mind' (RV 10.129.4); 'seed-placers' in 10.129.5.
Desire, which arose in the beginning as the first seed of mind (RV 10.129.4; AVŚ 19.52.1).

The cosmic Person, thousand-headed, who is all this, of whom one quarter is all beings and three quarters the immortal in heaven, and from whose sacrifice the world, Vedas and varṇas came (RV 10.90); the person in whom the gods dwell 'as cows in a stall' (AVŚ 11.8.32).

notes: Other lineages (e.g. Sāṃkhya) contribute very different definitions under this term; no equivalence is asserted here.

definitions.definition: The Golden Germ that arose in the beginning as the one lord of what exists (RV 10.121.1).

equivalents.note: The last verse of RV 10.121 answers the refrain with 'Prajāpati'; the Anukramaṇī names the deity Ka (Prajāpati).

definitions.definition: The lord of creatures, named in the last verse of the Hiraṇyagarbha hymn (RV 10.121.10) and in the White Yajurveda as moving unborn within the womb and born in many ways (VS 31.19); in the Atharvaveda Time is his father (AVŚ 19.53.8).
The All-maker who forged heaven and earth, with eyes, faces, arms and feet everywhere, the one name-giver of the gods (RV 10.81–82).
The support or frame of the universe in which tapas, ṛta, vows, faith and truth abide, identified with the highest Brahman (AVŚ 10.7).

equivalents.note: AVŚ 10.7.17 joins knowing Brahman in man, the highest Brahman and Skambha.

definitions.definition: The highest Brahman to which homage is paid as presiding over past, future and all (AVŚ 10.8.1; 10.7.32–34).

equivalents.note: The Atharvaveda's 'highest Brahman' is the nearest Saṃhitā use to the Upaniṣadic Brahman.

definitions.definition: The remainder of the sacrifice, praised as the ground in which name and form and all the world rest (AVŚ 11.7).
Time as the first god and lord of all, father of Prajāpati, from whom the waters, brahman, tapas and the Vedas arose (AVŚ 19.53–54).
The feminine principle from whom the Puruṣa was born and who was born from him (RV 10.90.5); in the Atharvaveda she was all this in the beginning and was milked by gods, men and others (AVŚ 8.10).
The red (rising) sun praised as a creative supreme power in Atharvaveda book 13.
Name and form, which are placed in the Remainder (AVŚ 11.7.1).
The wondrous creative power by which Varuṇa measured out the earth (RV 5.85.5) and Indra goes in many forms (6.47.18); the wise see the bird 'anointed with the asura's māyā' (10.177.1).

notes: Other lineages (Advaita, Śaiva, Buddhist) contribute very different definitions of māyā; the Vedic sense is creative, wondrous power. The Bṛhadāraṇyaka (2.5.19) quotes RV 6.47.18.

definitions.definition: The highest heaven, where the syllable rests on which the gods sit (RV 1.164.39), where the dead meet the fathers (10.14.8), and where the overseer of creation is (10.129.7).
Viṣṇu's highest step, which the wise ever see and where there is a well-spring of honey (RV 1.22.20, 1.154.5).

notes: The Kaṭha Upaniṣad (1.3.9) names it the end of the road (reference only).

definitions.definition: Step, place, quarter (speech has four padas, RV 1.164.45) and, in recitation, the word (as in padapāṭha).
The syllable in the highest heaven on which the verses rest and the gods sit (RV 1.164.39); the thousand-syllabled cow of speech (1.164.41).
The fourth quarter of speech, the only one humans speak; the other three are hidden (RV 1.164.45).

notes: The Māṇḍūkya Upaniṣad's turīya (the fourth state) is contributed by U03; any link between the two is interpretive and not asserted here.

definitions.definition: The swan seated in the bright, in men, in ṛta, in the sky (RV 4.40.5); in the Atharvaveda the swan rising from the waters that never lifts one foot is Prāṇa (AVŚ 11.4.21).

Breath and self: Sūrya is the self of what moves and stands (RV 1.115.1); the dead man's breath (ātman) goes to the wind (10.16.3); Vāta is the self of the gods (10.168.4); knowing the wise, ageless, young self one does not fear death (AVŚ 10.8.44).
The life-breath that leaves at death (the fathers 'have gone to asu', RV 10.15.1); the one life of the gods arose from the waters (10.121.7).
Breath and life-force; in the Atharvaveda Prāṇa is lord of all, death and fever, awake among sleepers (AVŚ 11.4); wind was born from the Puruṣa's breath (RV 10.90.13).
Out-breath, named with prāṇa in the Saṃhitā lists of breaths (TS 4.7; AVŚ 8.1, 15.16).
The diffused breath, the third of the breaths named in the Saṃhitās (TS 4.7; AVŚ 15.15–17).
The up-breath, named with the other breaths in some Saṃhitā and Brāhmaṇa lists (low confidence for particular Saṃhitā loci).
The equalizing breath, named with the other breaths in later Vedic lists (low confidence for particular Saṃhitā loci).

Mind: the swiftest of flying things (RV 6.9.5); the divine mind that goes far in waking and returns in sleep, the one light of lights, heart-seated charioteer (VS 34.1–6); it can wander to Yama and be called back (RV 10.58); desire was its first seed (10.129.4).
The visionary thought or insight of the seer, which is 'yoked' (RV 5.81.1) and which Savitṛ is asked to impel (3.62.10).
Effective will and resolve; 'may auspicious intentions come from all sides' (RV 1.89.1); the gods go toward one kratu (6.9.5).
The inspired wisdom with which the seers searched their hearts (RV 10.129.4).
Wisdom and retentive intelligence, invoked as a goddess by students (AVŚ 6.108; 1.1).

The heart as the place of inner seeing: the seers searched in the heart (RV 10.129.4); the light is set in the heart (6.9.6); the wise see with heart and mind (10.177.1); the mind is heart-seated (VS 34.6).
Light — the highest light reached by the worshipper (RV 1.50.10), the light set in the heart (6.9.5–6), the light reached by soma-drinkers (8.48.3), the light of lights that is mind (VS 34.1).

The wondrous presence, 'endowed with self' (ātmanvat), within the golden sheath or nine-gated lotus, known by the knowers of Brahman (AVŚ 10.2.32, 10.8.43); the mind is the unprecedented yakṣa within creatures (VS 34.2).

literal: the unborn part (or: the goat as portion)

definitions.definition: What Agni is asked to heat and carry to the world of the well-doers at cremation (RV 10.16.4); read either as the dead man's unborn part or as the goat offered as Agni's portion.
Strand: the nine-gated lotus is 'covered with three strands' (AVŚ 10.8.43).

notes: The Sāṃkhya sense (three qualities) is contributed by other units; identifying the two is a later reading (see interpretation_log).

definitions.definition: A region of space, especially the atmosphere; 'there was no rajas' before creation (RV 10.129.1); the six rajāṃsi propped apart (1.164.6).

notes: The later guṇa sense is contributed by other units.

definitions.definition: Speech as goddess and power: she proclaims herself queen and self of all (RV 10.125); four quarters of her, three hidden (1.164.45); she revealed herself to some like a bride (10.71.4); the gods begot her and all animals speak her (8.100.11).

equivalents.note: Bhartṛhari's 'Brahman as word' is a later philosophy of sound that draws on the Vedic exaltation of Vāc; the Saṃhitās do not use the term.

definitions.definition: A Vedic verse or formula used in rite and recitation; its meaningfulness was defended by Yāska against Kautsa (Nirukta 1.15–16); in the Saṃhitā 'common be your mantra (counsel)' (RV 10.191.3).

notes: Scholarly metadata only (not used in interpretation): cognate of Avestan maθra.

definitions.definition: A metrical verse of praise, the unit of the Ṛgveda; the verses rest on the syllable in the highest heaven (RV 1.164.39); ṛc is speech (VS 36.1).
A melody sung on a verse by the udgātṛ priests; the Sāmaveda; sāman is breath (VS 36.1).
A (mostly prose) sacrificial formula spoken by the adhvaryu while acting; the Yajurveda; yajus is mind (VS 36.1).
The continuous text of a Veda (with sandhi), and the collection itself (Ṛg-, Sāma-, Yajur-, Atharva-saṃhitā).
A branch or recension of a Veda handed down in a teacher-line; Vyāsa's pupils branched the Vedas through their pupils (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 1.4.23).
A school of Vedic study and ritual practice, often coextensive with a śākhā and its sūtras.
A hymn of the Ṛg- or Atharvaveda.
One of the ten books of the Ṛgveda.
A lesson or section, the recitation unit of the Ṛgveda (within maṇḍalas) and of the Taittirīya texts.
A supplementary hymn transmitted with a Saṃhitā but not counted in it.
The eleven supplementary hymns printed as RV 8.49–59.
The recitation of a Saṃhitā word by word, with sandhi undone.
Recitation of overlapping word pairs (ab, bc, cd …).
Recitation in which each pair is said forward, backward and forward (ab ba ab, bc cb bc …).
The most complex common recitation (ab ba abc cba abc, …), guarding the order of every word.
The eight 'modified' recitations built on the krama: jaṭā, mālā, śikhā, rekhā, dhvaja, daṇḍa, ratha, ghana.
Vedic pitch-accent (udātta, anudātta, svarita) and, in the Sāmaveda, the seven notes of chant; a mantra wrong in svara harms the sacrificer (Pāṇinīya Śikṣā 52).
The raised (high) accent.
The low accent.
The falling (circumflex) accent following an udātta.
Vedic metre; the metres came from the Puruṣa sacrifice (RV 10.90.9).
The metre of three eight-syllable lines, and the Sāvitrī verse in it (RV 3.62.10), repeated with the vyāhṛtis (VS 36.3).
The metre of four eleven-syllable lines, the commonest of the Ṛgveda.
The metre of four twelve-syllable lines.
The metre of four eight-syllable lines (the Puruṣa Sūkta's metre), later the śloka.
The deity addressed by a verse, recorded with its seer and metre in the Anukramaṇīs; in the person 'all deities dwell as cows in a stall' (AVŚ 11.8.32).
The ritual application of a mantra, stated with its seer, metre and deity before recitation.
An index of seers, deities, metres and hymns of a Veda (e.g. the Sarvānukramaṇī).
The three Vedas (Ṛg, Yajus, Sāman) as the knowledge of the śrauta rite; the Atharvaveda's place beside them was debated.
The Veda as heard revelation, transmitted by hearing from teacher to pupil.
The Veda as not composed by any person; the named seers saw or first transmitted it.

notes: The term is Mīmāṃsā's (U12); the Saṃhitā lineage's self-understanding is recorded here with the counter-evidence of 'fashioned' hymns (dsp:seen-or-made-hymns).

definitions.definition: A verse-book of the Sāmaveda (Pūrvārcika, Uttarārcika), the texts on which the melodies are sung.
A Sāmaveda song-book giving the verses transformed into melodies.

literal: to be sung in the village

definitions.definition: The melodies sung in the village (public ritual).

literal: to be sung in the forest

definitions.definition: The melodies sung in the forest, regarded as more potent and secret.
The adaptation of a base melody to new verses in the order of the rites.
The secret (rahasya) song-book applying forest melodies to ritual verse-groups.
Non-lexical syllables or words (e.g. hāu, hoyi, ā) inserted in a sāman.
The central portion of a sāman, sung by the udgātṛ.
The opening portion of a sāman, sung by the prastotṛ.
The portion of a sāman sung by the pratihartṛ.
The fourth portion of a five-part sāman, sung by the udgātṛ.
The closing portion of a sāman, sung by all three chanters.
The humming sound 'hiṃ' preceding a sāman.
One of the two principal sāmans of the soma rite, forming part of the Vrātya's seat (AVŚ 15.3).
The other principal sāman of the soma rite, paired with the rathantara (AVŚ 15.3).
The ritual exchange of riddles on cosmic matters (VS 23.9–12); RV 1.164 is composed in this manner.
The utterances bhūḥ, bhuvaḥ, svaḥ, recited before the Gāyatrī (VS 36.3; cf. 3.5).

The sacred syllable, which in the Saṃhitā layer appears at the close of the Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā ('Oṃ, kratu, remember'; 'Oṃ, the void is brahman', VS 40.15–17) and as the first of the four quarters of speech in one reading (Nirukta 13.9).
Peace and the appeasing of what is harmful; the peace chants (VS 36.17; AVŚ 19.9).
Soma as it flows through the filter; the ninth maṇḍala.
A seer of the hymns; 'a ṛṣi is so called from seeing' (Nirukta 2.11); the seers had direct perception of dharma (1.20); Vāc makes whom she loves a ṛṣi (RV 10.125.5).
A woman seer of Ṛgveda verses (e.g. Lopāmudrā, Ghoṣā, Apālā, Viśvavārā, Vāc Āmbhṛṇī), recorded in the Anukramaṇīs.
The women named in the Bṛhaddevatā as speakers of Vedic verses.
The seven seers; in RV 10.137 Bharadvāja, Kaśyapa, Gotama, Atri, Viśvāmitra, Jamadagni and Vasiṣṭha each contribute a healing verse.
An inspired poet-sage, one who sees and speaks what is hidden (RV 10.129.4, 1.164.6).
An inspired poet or priest (RV 1.164.46; 10.114.5).
The silent sage of the Keśin hymn, wind-girdled and clad in soiled brown, ecstatic with munihood (RV 10.136).
The long-haired one who bears fire, poison-drink, heaven and earth and is called light (RV 10.136.1); the Anukramaṇī names the keśins Agni, Sūrya and Vāyu.
The state of the muni, by which the sages were 'exhilarated' and mounted the winds (RV 10.136.3).

literal: one bound by a vow / of a band

definitions.definition: The vow-bound wanderer of Atharvaveda book 15 who stirs Prajāpati, becomes Mahādeva and Īśāna, and is honoured as guest.
The Vrātya become sole lord (AVŚ 15.1.6).
The Vedic student, praised in AVŚ 11.5 as quickening both worlds by fuel, girdle, toil and tapas.
The teacher who, initiating the student, bears him three nights as an embryo (AVŚ 11.5.3).
Initiation of the student by the teacher (AVŚ 11.5.3, 'upanayamāna').
The solemn Vedic sacrifices performed with three fires and priests of the four Vedas.
The priest who recites the Ṛgveda verses; Agni is the divine hotṛ (RV 1.1.1).

notes: Scholarly metadata only (not used in interpretation): cognate of Avestan zaotar.

definitions.definition: The priest who performs the ritual actions speaking the Yajus formulas.
The priest who sings the sāmans.
The priest who oversees the whole rite in silence and repairs its faults; Vāc makes whom she loves a brahmán (RV 10.125.5).

notes: The Atharvavedic tradition claims this office for Atharvavedins (dsp:atharvaveda-status).

definitions.definition: An officiating priest; the full soma rite has sixteen in four groups of four (hotṛ, adhvaryu, udgātṛ, brahmán and their assistants).
The patron of the sacrifice who bears its cost and receives its fruit.
The western, household fire of the three śrauta fires.
The eastern fire into which oblations are offered.
The southern fire, associated with the fathers and protection.
The altar ground strewn with grass between the fires.
The strewn grass on which the gods are invited to sit.
That which is offered into the fire.
The call with which oblations are given to the gods.
The hotṛ's exclamation at the moment of offering.
The post to which the victim is tied in the animal sacrifice.
The plant, its pressed juice drunk in the sacrifice, and the god: 'we have drunk the soma, we have become immortal' (RV 8.48.3); but the soma the brahmins know none eats (10.85.3).

notes: Scholarly metadata only (not used in interpretation): cognate of Avestan haoma; the plant's botanical identity is debated by modern scholars and was replaced by substitutes in the tradition.

definitions.definition: The exhilaration of soma (RV 9.1.1 'most exhilarating'; 10.119).
Bliss produced by soma (RV 9.113.6) and dwelling in the immortal world (9.113.11).
Immortality and the immortal: of the gods, of the fathers' world, of soma; 'may I be freed from death, not from immortality' (RV 7.59.12).

equivalents.note: The Saṃhitās' immortality is chiefly full life and the immortal world of light; the Upaniṣads and Vedānta distinguish mokṣa from heavenly immortality. Recorded as contested.

definitions.definition: Heaven (svar), the world of light reached by sacrifice, gifts and tapas (RV 10.154.2).

equivalents.note: The Mīmāṃsā treats heaven as the highest human end of ritual; the Upaniṣads and later schools hold heaven impermanent and distinct from liberation.

definitions.definition: A world or realm: the world of the living, of the fathers, of the well-doers, the immortal world (RV 9.113.7).
The world of the living to which the widow is bidden to rise (RV 10.18.8).
The dead ancestors, lower, higher and middle, who have gone to the life-breath and rejoice with Yama in svadhā (RV 10.14–15).
The path of the gods, distinct from death's own path (RV 10.18.1) and from the fathers' (10.88.15).
The path of the fathers, one of the two paths 'I have heard of' (RV 10.88.15).
Yama son of Vivasvant, first mortal to die, who found the path for many and is king of the dead in the highest heaven (RV 10.14).

notes: Scholarly metadata only (not used in interpretation): cognate of Avestan Yima.

definitions.definition: Death as a power with its own path (RV 10.18.1) and fetters (AVŚ 8.1); 'may I be freed from death, not from immortality' (RV 7.59.12).
Destruction and misfortune personified, from whose lap and fetters one is rescued (RV 10.18.10; AVŚ 8.1.3).
The flesh-eating cremation fire sent away to Yama's realm after the cremation (RV 10.16.9).
Fire and the god of fire: household priest and messenger between men and gods, carrier of oblations, present in all fires, guardian of ṛta (RV 1.1).
The warrior king of the gods, soma-drinker, slayer of Vṛtra who released the waters (RV 1.32); some doubted him, and he answered 'here I am' (8.100.3–4).

notes: Scholarly metadata only (not used in interpretation): an Indra appears among the demons of the Avesta.

definitions.definition: Sovereign guardian of ṛta and the vows, all-seeing judge who binds with fetters and forgives (RV 7.86–89; AVŚ 4.16).
Varuṇa's companion, god of alliance; 'may we look on one another with the eye of Mitra (a friend)' (VS 36.18).

notes: Scholarly metadata only (not used in interpretation): cognate of Avestan Miθra.

definitions.definition: Mother of the Ādityas, before whom one prays to be sinless (RV 1.24.15); born of Dakṣa, and Dakṣa of her (10.72.4).
The sons of Aditi (Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman and others), who stand by ṛta (RV 10.85.1).
The fierce archer-god feared for his arrows and loved as the best physician, lord of cattle, 'auspicious' (śiva), praised in hundreds of forms in the Śatarudrīya.
The storm-gods, sons of Rudra (RV 2.33.1).
The god of the three strides, whose highest step the wise ever see (RV 1.22.20, 1.154).
The Sun, eye of Mitra and Varuṇa, 'the self of what moves and stands' (RV 1.115.1).
The god who impels, to whom the Gāyatrī is addressed (RV 3.62.10) and who first yoked the mind (VS 11.1).
The Dawn, ever returning while generations of mortals pass (RV 1.113.11).
The twin horsemen, divine physicians and rescuers, praised by Ghoṣā (RV 10.39–40).
Lord of sacred speech (brahmaṇaspati), who smelted the worlds like a smith (RV 10.72.2) and is addressed in the hymn on knowledge (10.71).
The Wind, 'the breath of the gods, germ of the world', whose sounds are heard, not his form (RV 10.168.4).
The rain-god, 'father' beside mother Earth (AVŚ 12.1.12).
The guide on the paths who leads the dead to the fathers (RV 10.17.3–6).
The divine craftsman who shapes forms and grants long life (RV 10.18.6).
River-goddess, later goddess of speech; the Anukramaṇī gives her as deity of RV 1.164.49.
Heaven, paired with Earth.
The Earth, mother of men (AVŚ 12.1.12), upheld by truth, order, consecration, tapas, brahman and sacrifice (12.1.1), to whom the dead are returned (RV 10.18.10).
A name of the One named in RV 1.164.46; the messenger who brought fire.
The serpent who enclosed the waters and was slain by Indra (RV 1.32).

notes: Scholarly metadata only (not used in interpretation): cf. Avestan vərəθraγna (victory).

definitions.definition: In the Ṛgveda a lord of mysterious power, applied to Varuṇa and other gods ('great is the one asura-ship of the gods', RV 3.55); later the gods' opponents.

notes: Scholarly metadata only (not used in interpretation): cognate of Avestan ahura.

definitions.definition: A god; thirty-three in heaven, earth and waters (RV 1.139.11) or 3,339 (3.9.9).

notes: Scholarly metadata only (not used in interpretation): cognate of Avestan daēva (demon).

definitions.definition: Demonic beings who harm the rite and cause disease, driven off by Agni and the healer (RV 10.97.6).
A sorcerer or demon; Vasiṣṭha swears he is none (RV 7.104.15).
The Yajurveda Saṃhitās in which mantra and explanatory prose are mixed (Taittirīya, Maitrāyaṇī, Kāṭhaka, Kapiṣṭhala).
The Vājasaneyi Yajurveda, whose Saṃhitā holds the mantras apart from the Brāhmaṇa; received by Yājñavalkya from the Sun.
The litany of homage to Rudra in his hundreds of forms (TS 4.5; VS 16).
The Śatarudrīya, named from its repeated 'namaḥ' (homage).
The litany of petitions 'and … for me' (TS 4.7; VS 18).
The formula 'namaḥ śivāya', which the Śaiva traditions trace to the eighth section of the Śatarudrīya (TS 4.5.8).

notes: U01 contribution: the Vedic locus only. Śaiva units contribute the mantra's doctrine and practice.

definitions.definition: The god (Rudra) of the verse 'we worship Tryambaka … may I be freed from death, not from immortality' (RV 7.59.12; TS 1.8.6; VS 3.60).
Epithet of Rudra in the Śatarudrīya (TS 4.5.1; VS 16.8).
Epithet of Rudra as lord of beasts, to whom the five kinds of animals are allotted (AVŚ 11.2); also in the Śatarudrīya.
In the Saṃhitās an adjective of Rudra's auspicious, non-terrible form (TS 4.5.1) and a name in 'namaḥ śivāya ca śivatarāya ca' (TS 4.5.8); Rudra 'auspicious, go beyond' (VS 3.61).
Epithet of Rudra (RV 1.114; VS 16).
A name of Rudra, paired with Śarva (AVŚ 11.2).
A name of Rudra, paired with Bhava (AVŚ 11.2).
Lord; the Vrātya 'became Īśāna' (AVŚ 15.1.5); a name of Rudra.
A remedy — plants, waters, amulets and spells; Rudra has a thousand (RV 7.46.3); 'the waters are the remedy for all' (10.137.6).
Rudra's healing remedy (RV 1.43.4, 2.33.7).
The primordial fire-priest who churned out Agni (RV 6.16.13); with the Aṅgirases, the seers of the Atharvaveda.

notes: Scholarly metadata only (not used in interpretation): cognate of Avestan āθravan (priest).

definitions.definition: The Aṅgirases, ancient priestly clan; with the Atharvans the Atharvaveda is 'Atharvāṅgirasaḥ'.
The old name of the Atharvaveda, pairing its auspicious (ātharvaṇa) and fierce (āṅgirasa) portions.
The Atharvaveda's healing rites and hymns against fever, consumption, jaundice, leprosy, worms and demons.
An amulet (of wood, plant or other material) bound on with Atharvaveda hymns for protection and healing.
A harmful spell or effigy sent by an enemy, turned back by counter-rites.
Hostile sorcery; one class of Atharvavedic rites.
Rites and hymns for long life (AVŚ 8.1–2; VS 3.62).
Rites for prosperity (increase of cattle, crops, wealth).
Expiatory rite for faults in ritual or conduct.
Fever, especially the recurring fever, sent away by Atharvavedic charms (AVŚ 5.22); Prāṇa is also called takman (11.4.11).
Consumption or disease generally, driven out by Atharvavedic hymns (AVŚ 3.7).
An inherited or chronic disease (AVŚ 3.7).
White spots of the skin, treated with the dark plant (AVŚ 1.23–24).
Worms in body and animals, destroyed by charms (AVŚ 2.32).
The year, born from the ocean (RV 10.190.2), the twelve-spoked wheel with 720 sons (1.164.11) or 360 spokes (1.164.48).
A season; spring, summer and autumn were ghee, fuel and oblation in the Puruṣa sacrifice (RV 10.90.6).
An age or generation; 'in the earliest age of the gods being was born from non-being' (RV 10.72.2).

notes: The later cycle of four yugas is contributed by other units.

definitions.definition: The atmosphere between earth and heaven, the middle of the three worlds.
Heaven and earth as a pair.
Deceit and injurious intent; wrongs against the gods (RV 7.86.5 'drugdhāni').

notes: Scholarly metadata only (not used in interpretation): cognate of Avestan druj (the Lie).

definitions.definition: Crooked conduct, which Varuṇa and the Ādityas see beside the straight.
Kind and true speech, among the goods asked in the Camaka (TS 4.7).

In the Ṛgveda, the potent sacred formulation or prayer and the power in it (Bṛhaspati/Brahmaṇaspati is its lord); in the Atharvaveda and Yajurveda, the highest principle: 'that is brahman' (VS 32.1), 'homage to the highest Brahman' (AVŚ 10.8.1), 'those who know Brahman in man know the Supreme' (10.7.17), Brahman entered the golden city of the body (10.2.33).

notes: U01 contribution: the Saṃhitā senses. The Upaniṣadic and Vedānta definitions are contributed by other units.
